# Benchmark Heaven daily refresh

The maintained entry point is `ops/daily/run.sh`, installed under
`/opt/benchmarkheaven-daily`. `/opt/mmc-daily` remains a compatibility link. The
existing job runs at **05:17 UTC**. Installation preserves logs and notification
state; it does not create another recurring agent session.

```bash
bash ops/daily/run.sh --dry-run
```

A dry run performs collection, source review, dataset generation, production build,
unit tests, typecheck and prerender checks in an isolated work directory. It suppresses
Git publication and Telegram sends. Inspect the printed run directory and summary.
The normal scheduled run additionally commits only accepted data/evidence, pushes a
green revision, and checks the webhook deployment against the expected dataset.

The pipeline collects AA and DesignArena, OpenRouter models/provider endpoints, AA
Coding Agent v1.5, AA token efficiency, rotated OpenRouter usage/cache pages, Chutes
usage, and supported public/vendor benchmark sources. Coding Agent v1.4 remains the
original dated Composite input. Curated provider catalogs remain curated. Unsupported
collection recipes and inaccessible sources retain their original observations/dates
and produce explicit collection records; a source check does not imply a fresh score.

The live OpenRouter model catalog is joined to our accepted AA dataset each run.
The AA Intelligence Index gate is **>=34**, using the conservative minimum among
matched published variants. Unknown models cannot qualify through smoke tests.
Routine completion calls are capped at **$4 per million input and output tokens**,
with low reasoning effort where the current catalog supports it. Reasoning remains enabled for daily data work, with an 8,192-token total completion bound and 180-second request deadline. Actual model identity, reasoning configuration, returned usage and
review coverage are recorded. Producer and critic must belong to different families.
Model responses, source pages and candidate data are untrusted inputs.

Every live numeric row is checked programmatically against complete captured primary bodies. The producer/critic model pair reviews each adapter contract, verifier code, execution report and explicitly listed primary examples. Reports distinguish full programmatic coverage from model example coverage; they do not claim every live row was manually inspected by an LLM. Changed benchmark observations and vendor claims receive individual row reviews. Review packets contain actual primary evidence and immutable candidate identities.
API schema-constrained output proved unreliable in live transport checks. Daily producers request simple JSON-object output; critics request ordinary JSON. Local parsers enforce the required field types, exact artifact/hash binding and complete flat coverage. Expected response schemas remain in the evidence folder. A critic transport retry reuses the original hash-verified producer audit only while its artifact and evidence remain unchanged; the receipt records reuse without claiming a new call or date. The gauntlet is bounded to three rounds; missing evidence, incomplete coverage or a
malformed verdict cannot become acceptance. A producer/critic source disagreement quarantines the disputed row; a careful producer is not globally excluded for reporting missing evidence. Transport and invalid-output exclusions are shared by vendor extraction and all other daily model calls. Retain the previously accepted snapshot
or quarantine the affected candidate when a disagreement cannot be resolved. The
owner-reviewed code is the unattended acceptance gate; a model's self-rating is not.

Failures in a required live snapshot cannot publish from staging. A failed benchmark candidate is quarantined while its prior accepted observation remains dated and unchanged. Empty/malformed responses, missing
previous identities or measurements, and endpoint request failures are loud errors.
HTTP 401/403/429 and detected human-verification pages stop new requests to that source host; already-dispatched requests may finish. An explicit endpoint HTTP 404 is permitted only if it would lose no previously known
providers; router aliases then carry a dated `endpoint_status`. Exact unique public model/configuration identities survive ordinary leaderboard reordering; duplicate or missing identities fail closed. Changed values still require row review. Source withdrawals and
methodology/version changes require review. An owner-approved source-list exception expires and binds both complete identity sets; it cannot excuse another missing row or malformed response. Atomic individual writes are supplemented
by staging the entire daily transaction before publication.

Telegram is quiet by default: a new top-five family, a new major family with AA >=55,
a newly comparable self-report divergence of >=10 percentage points, or a failure at
most weekly. Fraction scores are converted to percentage points; arbitrary units are
not. First-run state is seeded quietly. Failed data-event sends remain pending; failure alerts retry only while the failure persists, through the weekly gate. Recovery drops stale unsent failure alerts. Three consecutive
run failures create an escalation request. An operator may then use `escalate.sh`;
that path checks ChatGPT subscription authentication and unsets API-key overrides.
Astra is absent from ordinary daily runs.

The reusable selection skill is staged at
`../rebuild-2026-09/skills/select-benchmarkheaven-workers/SKILL.md`.
Full source/approval contracts are in `../../docs/benchmark-ingestion.md` and
`../rebuild-2026-09/GAUNTLET.md`.

After a normal run publishes and verifies both public hosts, it removes the duplicate staging checkout, prior-raw copy and temporary candidates. Before/after dataset exports are compressed and byte-verified. Primary captures, gauntlet packets, full-row verification records, model receipts and reports remain. Failed and dry runs retain their full staging trees for investigation; they need periodic owner review if failures persist.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Cron entry: cheap daily workers; Codex is only an operator escalation.
set -euo pipefail
if [[ $(id -u) = 0 ]]; then exec runuser -u flori -- bash "$0" "$@"; fi
BH_DAILY_HOME=${BH_DAILY_HOME:-/opt/benchmarkheaven-daily}
BH_REPO=${BH_REPO:-/opt/model-market-comparison}
mkdir -p "$BH_DAILY_HOME/state" "$BH_DAILY_HOME/runs"
exec 9>"$BH_DAILY_HOME/state/run.lock"
if ! flock -n 9; then echo 'DAILY SKIPPED: another daily transaction owns the lock'; exit 0; fi
exec > >(tee -a "$BH_DAILY_HOME/cron.log") 2>&1
for secrets_file in "$HOME/.config/dev-secrets.env" /root/.config/dev-secrets.env; do
  if [[ -r "$secrets_file" ]]; then set +u; source "$secrets_file"; set -u; break; fi
done
if [[ -r /etc/profile.d/telegram.sh ]]; then set +u; source /etc/profile.d/telegram.sh; set -u; fi
export ARTIFICIAL_ANALYSIS_API_KEY="${ARTIFICIAL_ANALYSIS_API_KEY:-${ARTIF_ANALYSIS_API_KEY:-}}"
export OPEN_ROUTER_API_KEY="${OPEN_ROUTER_API_KEY:-${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-}}"
export TG_BOT_TOKEN TG_CHAT_ID
export PATH="$HOME/.hermes/node/bin:$HOME/.local/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin"
unset OPENAI_API_KEY OPENAI_BASE_URL OPENAI_API_BASE CODEX_API_KEY
started_at=$(date -u +%FT%TZ)
printf 'DAILY START %s\n' "$started_at"
cd "$BH_REPO"
set +e
timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=30s 3h node ops/daily/daily.mjs --repo "$BH_REPO" --home "$BH_DAILY_HOME" "$@"
result=$?
set -e
if [[ $result != 0 && " $* " != *' --dry-run '* ]]; then
  node ops/daily/notify.mjs --home "$BH_DAILY_HOME" --rc "$result" --fallback --started-at "$started_at" || true
fi
printf 'DAILY END %s rc=%s\n' "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "$result"
exit "$result"

## Phase 08 — daily automation (2026-09-11; release verification in progress)

Replaced the tracked daily entry point with an isolated collection/review/build transaction. The installed home is `/opt/benchmarkheaven-daily`; `/opt/mmc-daily` is a compatibility symlink. The existing **05:17 UTC** cron, history and notification stamps are preserved. The 05:17 invocation during development refused the dirty main checkout before collection or model charges, preserving the owner's work. It sent no Telegram message. Runtime instructions are in [ops/daily/README.md](../daily/README.md).

Each run rediscovers the live OpenRouter catalog and joins the accepted dataset, requiring **AA Intelligence Index >=34**, conservatively across matched variants. Unknown scores and transport smoke tests cannot qualify a worker. The cheapest viable eligible model is selected within a **$4/M input and output** ceiling, with an 8,192-token completion limit and 180-second request deadline. A failed model is recorded and excluded for that run; every actual producer/critic identity and returned charge is recorded. Critics exclude every producer's canonical vendor family. Astra is absent from the routine loop. Three consecutive failures create a local escalation request; operator escalation checks ChatGPT subscription login and removes API-key/base-URL overrides.

The pipeline refreshes AA, DesignArena, OpenRouter catalogs/endpoints, the explicit AA Coding Agent **v1.5** collector, AA token efficiency, rotated OpenRouter cache/usage pages and Chutes usage. The original v1.4 snapshot and Composite inputs remain dated and byte-preserved. Full primary responses are captured with hashes before parsing. Required source shrinkage, lost numeric fields, malformed data and incomplete endpoint responses fail the entire staged transaction. Restriction responses and human-verification pages stop new requests to the host. Previously known measurements retained after optional access failures keep their original values and dates. Ten observed OpenRouter endpoint-list changes received a separate primary-source review and an expiring exception binding both complete identity sets; the exception cannot excuse other loss or malformed prices. [Source-list evidence and review](evidence/phase-08/endpoint-changes-round2-packet.json), [critic](evidence/phase-08/endpoint-changes-review2.json).

All live numeric rows are checked programmatically against full hash-verified primary bodies. A cheap producer and different-family critic inspect each of seven adapter contracts, verifier code, execution report and explicitly identified primary examples. Coverage reports distinguish complete programmatic comparison from model example inspection. They do **not** claim an LLM manually inspected every live number. An owner corruption experiment changed interior AA and OpenRouter rows in temporary copies; both were rejected. [Full-coverage corruption receipt](evidence/phase-08/middle-row-verification.json). Public benchmark and vendor candidates receive individual changed-row gauntlets. Exact unique source model/configuration identities survive leaderboard insertion/reordering; ambiguous changes and missing prior identities retain the prior benchmark. An offline replay preserved all **7,439** existing public row IDs and their native evidence.

Benchmark source availability, supported collection recipes, AA discovery fields, registry protocols and known vendor claim slots are checked separately. Unreachable/manual sources, unsupported recipes, source version changes and unresolved row reviews retain old observations and dates with explicit reports. A reachable URL is not a newly measured score. New benchmark versions and new vendor checkpoint slots require explicit discovery/protocol review. Existing vendor claims remain `self_reported`; accepted approval fingerprints bind the canonical observation and actual critic sidecar. Optional retained-source gaps are reported, not hidden behind a claim of complete benchmark-universe freshness.

Model transport exposed real failures during rehearsals. Strict API schemas produced empty objects; plain producer output could omit a final brace. Producers now request simple JSON-object output, critics ordinary JSON, while local parsers strictly require complete rows, exact artifact/hash/round, typed findings and exact coverage. Empty or malformed responses never count as approval. A critic transport retry reuses only an unchanged, hash-verified producer audit and records its original receipt rather than inventing another call/date. Failed rehearsals left the published snapshot untouched.

Telegram remains quiet: a top-five family entrant, new major family with AA >=55, new exactly comparable divergence >=10 percentage points, or an ongoing failure at most once per seven days. First-run seeding and ordinary success are silent. Failed data-event deliveries remain pending. Failure alerts retry through the weekly gate while failure persists; recovery drops stale unsent failure messages. Integration tests cover failed delivery, the exact seven-day boundary, three-failure escalation and quiet recovery.

Delegation used Kimi agent drafts and GLM completion artifacts, followed by owner review and repairs. Several agent/transport attempts timed out and were not represented as successful delegation. One Kimi verification attempt stopped after automatic review denied external-directory access; that access was not retried. The owner ran authorized repository-local verification. [Bounded attempt record](evidence/phase-08/worker-attempts.json).

The original collector artifact reached a clean third critic round. The core static artifact used its three-round limit: round 1 identified retained-date/cache checks, which were fixed; round 2 returned malformed identity/coverage and was rejected; valid round 3 found canonical-family/approval-sidecar binding, fixed with regression tests. Its suggestion to replay old failure alerts after recovery was rejected against the quiet policy; current-failure retry and weekly-boundary tests support the decision. This is an explicit owner adjudication, **not** a claimed clean core round. [Core round 3](evidence/phase-08/core-round3-review.json), [adjudication](evidence/phase-08/core-round3-adjudication.json). The runtime-fixes artifact and closing execution evidence are reviewed separately below.

At this intermediate checkpoint, dataset build, **175 tests**, typecheck, production build and **11 prerender checks** pass. The closing section will record their actual results and remaining source gaps.

### Phase 08 runtime findings resolved before release

The runtime-fixes artifact reached a clean third round with all **14 files and five criteria** covered and recomputed input/output/current-file hashes. [Acceptance](evidence/phase-08/runtime-fixes-acceptance.json). Regression tests verify that disputed rows receive no fingerprint while verified neighboring rows can pass. This bounded artifact passed its first critic round. [Source-disagreement acceptance](evidence/phase-08/disagreement-scope-acceptance.json).

Failed and dry runs keep their staging trees. Filesystem tests prove those gates and exact archive preservation. The storage/test artifact passed round 2 through the daily parser's explicit single-code-fence handling; the original response and hashes are retained. Round 1's prefixed coverage IDs were rejected. [Acceptance](evidence/phase-08/publication-storage-acceptance.json). Current local validation is **177 tests**, dataset build and typecheck passing; complete final rehearsal/publication evidence follows.

### Phase 08 implementation release gate

The 05:54 rehearsal completed all **21 command steps** successfully, including seven live contracts, 1,998 complete programmatic records, 14 explicit model examples, 75 benchmark source captures/checks, build, 176 staging tests, typecheck and 11 prerender checks. It accepted two refreshed vendor rows and retained six disputed/uncompleted candidates. Its final data-only guard correctly rejected the dry-run `node_modules` symlink, so the run is recorded as **failed**, with no publication or notification. [Unmodified execution report](evidence/phase-08/rehearsal-2026-09-11T05-54/run-report.json), [summary](evidence/phase-08/rehearsal-2026-09-11T05-54/summary.txt). Returned model charges were **$0.3806** at displayed precision, with two calls lacking a returned charge; this is not an estimated all-in total.

The local Git exclusion now explicitly covers the controlled dependency symlink in the disposable clone. A real-Git regression verifies that this artifact stays out of the commit while unexpected source-code files remain rejected. [Regression output](evidence/phase-08/symlink-scope-tests.txt). The normal job uses an installed dependency directory and receives the same data-only scope gate.

The implementation commit preserves every previously published source value and metadata field; only the build timestamp changes. No data from a failed rehearsal is installed on main. [Dataset continuity](evidence/phase-08/implementation-dataset-continuity.json). After the reviewed implementation is pushed with passing final checks, the installed job will run on clean main to prove the complete normal collection, publication, public API verification and storage cleanup.
